claims.title: Founding of Erebuni
claims.summary: The Urartian king Argishti I founded the fortress of Erebuni on the site of present-day Yerevan, one of the oldest continuously inhabited city sites in the world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Armenia: From the kingdom of Urartu and the world's first Christian state through Ani and the genocide to a republic reborn in 1991.", terralore.co/country/ARM/chronicle#ev-782bce-founding-of-erebuni, claim TL:ARM:event:782bce:founding-of-erebuni, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Urartu at its height
claims.summary: In the 9th and 8th centuries BCE the kingdom of Urartu, centred on Lake Van, became a major power of the Middle East before being succeeded in the region by the Armenians.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Armenia: From the kingdom of Urartu and the world's first Christian state through Ani and the genocide to a republic reborn in 1991.", terralore.co/country/ARM/chronicle#ev-714bce-urartu-at-its-height, claim TL:ARM:event:714bce:urartu-at-its-height, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Tigranes the Great
claims.summary: Tigranes II expanded Armenia until it briefly stretched from the Caspian toward the Mediterranean, taking the title 'king of kings' and making Armenia the strongest state in the Roman East before Roman armies forced his retreat.

sources.label: Tigranes II the Great, king of Armenia

claims.title: End of the Armenian monarchy
claims.summary: The Sasanian Persians abolished the Arsacid kingdom of Armenia and ruled the territory through appointed officials, ending the ancient Armenian monarchy.

claims.title: Armenia adopts Christianity
claims.summary: King Tiridates III proclaimed Christianity the religion of his kingdom after his conversion by Gregory the Illuminator, making Armenia the first nation to adopt Christianity as its state religion.

sources.label: Cathedral and Churches of Echmiatsin and the Archaeological Site of Zvartnots

claims.title: Mother Cathedral of Echmiatsin
claims.summary: The earliest of Armenia's great domed churches, the Mother Cathedral of Echmiatsin, was traditionally built by Tiridates III and Gregory the Illuminator; it remains the seat of the Armenian Apostolic Church.

sources.label: Cathedral and Churches of Echmiatsin and the Archaeological Site of Zvartnots

claims.title: Mesrop Mashtots creates the Armenian alphabet
claims.summary: The scholar Mesrop Mashtots devised the 36-letter Armenian alphabet, enabling Scripture and literature in Armenian and launching a 5th-century golden age of writing and translation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Armenia: From the kingdom of Urartu and the world's first Christian state through Ani and the genocide to a republic reborn in 1991.", terralore.co/country/ARM/chronicle#ev-405-mesrop-mashtots-creates-the-armenian-alphabet, claim TL:ARM:event:405:mesrop-mashtots-creates-the-armenian-alphabet, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bagratid kingdom restored
claims.summary: Ashot I of the Bagratuni dynasty was recognised as king of Armenia by both the caliph and the Byzantine emperor, reviving an independent Armenian monarchy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Armenia: From the kingdom of Urartu and the world's first Christian state through Ani and the genocide to a republic reborn in 1991.", terralore.co/country/ARM/chronicle#ev-885-bagratid-kingdom-restored, claim TL:ARM:event:885:bagratid-kingdom-restored, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ani becomes the Bagratid capital
claims.summary: King Ashot III moved the capital to Ani, which flourished as a major medieval city known as the 'city of a thousand churches' for its cathedral and monastic architecture.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Armenia: From the kingdom of Urartu and the world's first Christian state through Ani and the genocide to a republic reborn in 1991.", terralore.co/country/ARM/chronicle#ev-961-ani-becomes-the-bagratid-capital, claim TL:ARM:event:961:ani-becomes-the-bagratid-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kingdom of Cilician Armenia
claims.summary: Leo II was crowned king Leo I, raising the Armenian principality in Cilicia to a kingdom that, allied with the Crusaders, lasted until its conquest by the Mamluks in 1375.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Armenia: From the kingdom of Urartu and the world's first Christian state through Ani and the genocide to a republic reborn in 1991.", terralore.co/country/ARM/chronicle#ev-1198-kingdom-of-cilician-armenia, claim TL:ARM:event:1198:kingdom-of-cilician-armenia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Cilician Armenia
claims.summary: The Mamluks of Egypt conquered the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, extinguishing the last independent medieval Armenian state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Armenia: From the kingdom of Urartu and the world's first Christian state through Ani and the genocide to a republic reborn in 1991.", terralore.co/country/ARM/chronicle#ev-1375-fall-of-cilician-armenia, claim TL:ARM:event:1375:fall-of-cilician-armenia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Russia annexes eastern Armenia
claims.summary: Following war with Persia, Russia annexed the eastern (Persian) Armenian lands, dividing the Armenian homeland between the Russian and Ottoman empires.

claims.title: The Armenian Genocide
claims.summary: From 24 April 1915 the Ottoman Young Turk government deported and massacred the empire's Armenian population in death marches toward the Syrian desert; widely recognised as the first genocide of the 20th century, with deaths estimated from roughly 600,000 to as many as 1.5 million.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Armenia: From the kingdom of Urartu and the world's first Christian state through Ani and the genocide to a republic reborn in 1991.", terralore.co/country/ARM/chronicle#ev-1915-the-armenian-genocide, claim TL:ARM:event:1915:the-armenian-genocide, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Republic of Armenia
claims.summary: As the Russian Empire collapsed, Armenians of the Caucasus declared an independent Republic of Armenia with its capital at Yerevan, the first modern Armenian state.

claims.title: Sovietisation of Armenia
claims.summary: Squeezed between Turkish nationalist forces and the advancing Red Army, the First Republic fell and Armenia was Sovietised, ending its short-lived independence.

claims.title: Armenian SSR established
claims.summary: The Transcaucasian federation was dissolved and Armenia became a separate union republic of the U.S.S.R., the Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic.

claims.title: Nagorno-Karabakh dispute erupts
claims.summary: The regional legislature of Nagorno-Karabakh, an Armenian-majority enclave within Soviet Azerbaijan, voted to join Armenia, triggering a conflict that escalated into open war.

claims.title: Spitak earthquake
claims.summary: A catastrophic earthquake struck northern Armenia around Spitak and Gyumri, killing tens of thousands and leaving hundreds of thousands homeless in the final Soviet years.

claims.title: Independence from the Soviet Union
claims.summary: Armenians approved independence by referendum and the Supreme Council declared secession from the U.S.S.R.; the United States recognised Armenia on 25 December 1991.

claims.title: First Nagorno-Karabakh War ceasefire
claims.summary: After fighting that left roughly 30,000 dead (estimate) and hundreds of thousands displaced, a 1994 ceasefire left Armenian forces in de facto control of Nagorno-Karabakh and adjacent districts.

claims.title: The Velvet Revolution
claims.summary: A peaceful protest movement led by Nikol Pashinyan brought down the governing elite and installed a new reform government, with Pashinyan elected prime minister.

claims.title: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
claims.summary: In a 44-day war Azerbaijan retook much of the territory around Nagorno-Karabakh; a Russian-brokered ceasefire on 9 November 2020 ended the fighting, with heavy casualties on both sides (estimates).
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Armenia: From the kingdom of Urartu and the world's first Christian state through Ani and the genocide to a republic reborn in 1991.", terralore.co/country/ARM/chronicle#ev-2020-second-nagorno-karabakh-war, claim TL:ARM:event:2020:second-nagorno-karabakh-war, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Azerbaijani offensive and the Karabakh exodus
claims.summary: An Azerbaijani offensive brought Nagorno-Karabakh fully under its control; within about a week well over 100,000 ethnic Armenians fled to Armenia, and the enclave's authorities were dissolved by 1 January 2024.
